short_answer: Bill Krackomberger is a real and well known professional bettor. He appeared in Showtime's series Action, and he sells picks on WagerTalk and through an iPhone app called KrackWins, published by Krack Enterprises LLC. In that narrow sense he is a legitimate seller.

Whether his paid picks make money for buyers is harder to say. WagerTalk shows strong runs, such as 109-73 for +50.4 units in the NFL since 14 Dec and 126-90 on NFL player props over the last 365 days, and its Who's Hot board had him on top for the last 3 and 7 days on 16 Nov 2026. These are kept and chosen by the store that sells his picks. We found no independent, complete log.

Buyer posts are few. App Store reviews are mostly warm, one forum buyer in Feb 2026 said his baseball picks were not worth it, and other forum users mainly passed his plays around. If you buy, buy short, skip the paid guarantee unless you want store credit, and record every pick with the price you got.

guarantee: On WagerTalk the guarantee is an extra cost option: his $25 NFL prop cost $38 with it. The site says that if the daily package "does not result in an overall profit across all included plays," the paid cash value is "credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." That is store credit, not cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold 'as is'" and that no refund is issued once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. The KrackWins App Store listing describes monthly subscriptions and a free trial that turns into $99.99 a month; we saw no guarantee there. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Bill Krackomberger is thin. Most of what exists is App Store reviews and forum users sharing his plays. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found a small set of buyer comments over 2021 to 2026. The KrackWins App Store page holds 62 ratings averaging 3.8 out of 5; the reviews shown are positive, praising real time plays and the discipline the app teaches, and one user says he won at about 60%. On TheRX forum in Dec 2025 and Feb 2026, users mostly passed his plays around and talked about a group buy of a year; one buyer said he followed the baseball picks for a month, tried again after the All Star break, and found them not worth the money. We found no complaints about billing or refunds and no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about his service.
An App Store reviewer said there was nothing negative about the app or the professional who runs it.
Another App Store reviewer said the app was "a lesson in discipline." A separate undated review said the user had won at about a 60% rate so far, and the developer thanked him in Jan 2023.
The App Store shows a 3.8 out of 5 average from 62 ratings. Apple shows only a few written reviews, so the lower ratings behind that average are not visible to us.
On TheRX, a user shared two of his bowl plays and listed his 2025 college football record as 70-56. Another user said he planned to buy a 5% play and report back; we did not see a follow up result.
A TheRX user asked whether anyone had his Super Bowl 5% play and floated a group buy of a full year for $1,188. A week later another user posted the Super Bowl plays.

In the same thread, a user who said he bought the service for baseball wrote that he quit after about a month, tried again after the All Star break with no improvement, and judged it not worth the money.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks and keeps the record, the Hot Streaks and the Who's Hot board that promote them. The store has a direct interest in how he looks.
The guarantee is sold by the same store and pays in store credit, which keeps a losing buyer spending there.
strengths: A real, publicly known bettor with years of media appearances.
WagerTalk shows his last 20 plays with the line and odds, and prices every package.
The bankroll guide on his profile explains how his percentage ratings convert into stake sizes.
concerns: No full, independent record. Every streak starts on a date the seller or store chose.
The paid guarantee returns credit, not cash, and WagerTalk says all sales are final.
App subscriptions run up to $499.99 a month and a free trial turns into $99.99 a month.
Few independent buyer posts, and the one detailed buyer account we found was negative.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. Player prop unders at -115 need more than 53% to break even.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Cancel app trials before they renew if you only want to test the picks.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: He is a real, well known professional bettor who sells picks on WagerTalk and through his KrackWins app, with published prices. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because the records we saw are kept or chosen by the seller, and we found no court or regulator action involving his pick service.
How much does Bill Krackomberger cost?

On 16 Nov 2026 WagerTalk sold one NFL prop for $25 ($38 guaranteed), passes from $39 a day to $1,999 a year, and season packages from $259 to $719. The KrackWins app lists plans from $99.99 to $499.99 a month.
Does Bill Krackomberger have a verified record?
No. WagerTalk shows streaks such as 109-73 in the NFL since 14 Dec and a last 20 table, all kept by the store that sells his picks. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get the plays of a known professional bettor in real time. What is unproven is whether his paid picks beat break even over hundreds of plays at the prices buyers actually get. The guarantee pays store credit only, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
